writeup.p: C11 selects an enchantment option in an open enchanting table: a byte window id and a byte button (0 top, 1 middle, 2 bottom). It is the only serverbound packet whose sole effect is triggering Container.enchantItem, and it is sent from the vanilla GUI through PlayerControllerMP.enchantItem. The server replies with S2FPacketSetSlot carrying the enchanted result plus XP and lapis deltas.

processEnchantItem gates on three conditions: the packet's window id must equal the player's openContainer.windowId, the container must report canCraft, and the player must not be a spectator. Only then does it call enchantItem(playerEntity, button), which re-derives the enchantment from the table's seed, validates the lapis and level cost against the real player state, applies the enchantment and calls detectAndSendChanges. Every cost check is server-side; the packet carries nothing but the two bytes.

There is no AutoEnchant module in the corpus; the hits are all plumbing. Rise 6.1.30 and Rise 6.2.4 expose sendEnchantItem in the script PacketAPI, Tenacity 6.0 lists C11 in PacketUtil.isClientPacket, and November Recode 2.0 maps C11PacketEnchantItem to wire id 0x11 in LuaEventPacket so its Lua scripting API can identify the packet by id instead of by class. Enchanting in all of these clients goes through the vanilla GUI, so the packet is never intercepted for spoofing.

The server re-validates everything, so the packet itself cannot grant free enchants; the historical abuse is ordering, not content. A client that clicks an enchant and a C0E window action in the same tick can race the slot sync, which is the dupe-era vector. Because the button byte indexes the table's three server-side options, sending a button with no matching cost is harmless: enchantItem simply fails the level check. Anti-cheats ignore C11 entirely.

overview: The enchanting-table selection packet. Zero modules in the corpus drive it; the hits are the Rise 6.x script PacketAPI enchant bridge, Tenacity's silent-send whitelist and November Recode 2.0's Lua packet-id map.
server_handling: processEnchantItem: window id match, canCraft check, spectator rejection, then Container.enchantItem which re-validates lapis and XP server-side. detectAndSendChanges pushes S2FPacketSetSlot with the enchanted stack. No rate limit beyond the container state machine.
protocol_notes: byte windowId + byte button on the wire. Valid only while an EnchantmentTable container is open; any other container makes the window id check fail. The button maps to the table's three server-side options, which are deterministic from the world seed and player position.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C11; the packet is fully server-validated and carries no movement or timing signal. The only server-side observable is the ordering relative to C0E transactions during rapid enchanting.

modules.name: PacketAPI (script bridge)
modules.purpose: Expose C11 construction to the scripting layer so scripts can select enchantments programmatically.
modules.how_it_works: sendEnchantItem(windowId, enchantment) and sendEnchantItem(enchantment) build the packet and send it via PacketUtil.send; the overload without a window id reads thePlayer.openContainer.windowId at call time.
modules.vanilla_hook: No event hook; direct PacketUtil.send from script code.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None. The server re-validates the selection, so scripts gain convenience, not an exploit.
modules.variations: Identical PacketAPI.java exists in Rise 6.1.30 with the same method bodies.

modules.name: PacketUtil (silent whitelist)
modules.purpose: Classify C11 as a legitimate client packet for Tenacity's packet routing helpers.
modules.how_it_works: isClientPacket includes C11PacketEnchantItem in the full play-state whitelist.
modules.vanilla_hook: Packet send helper, no event hook.
modules.variations: Same whitelist pattern as C10; the file covers every serverbound play packet.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket (script bridge)
modules.purpose: Expose the serverbound packet id space to the Lua scripting API: scripts receive a numeric packet id instead of the raw class.
modules.how_it_works: A static block maps every serverbound play packet class to its 1.8.9 wire id, C11PacketEnchantItem to 0x11. The constructor resolves the id from the EventPacket payload via getOrDefault (falling back to -1) and stamps a direction string ('out' for EventPacket.Out, 'in' otherwise); Lua event wrappers then pass the id and direction to scripts. The source comment explains the map exists because runtime obfuscation would break reflection-based lookups.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket.In/Out bus events translated into the Lua wrapper; no packet is constructed or sent here.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None: the wrapper only reads the packet class. Scripts that want to drive C11 still go through vanilla methods; the map is visibility, not control.
modules.variations: Parallel to Rise 6.x's PacketAPI sendEnchantItem bridge, but November Recode 2.0 only identifies packets; it does not expose a send helper for enchanting.

general_hooks: No module hooks C11 in the corpus; scripting access goes through PacketAPI (Rise 6.x) or the LuaEventPacket wrapper (November Recode 2.0), not packet events.
client_variations: Rise 6.x exposes it in the script API; Tenacity classifies it in a helper; November Recode 2.0 maps it in the Lua wrapper. Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Rise 5.99 and Tenacity all send it only via the vanilla PlayerControllerMP.enchantItem path.
